title: Resume engine beta code review

messages.text:
You are acting as the senior developer on a small production codebase, doing the final code review before this program goes to its first beta test with a real user. Nothing ships to beta until you sign off. Be direct about problems — this is a pre-launch gate, not a courtesy pass.

PROJECT LOCATION: C:\Users\aaron\resume-engine

WHAT THIS PROGRAM DOES
It generates a tailored, designed resume PDF (plus an ATS-safe .docx) from a pasted job posting. All content originates from one source of truth, corpus/master-resume.yaml — a structured file of every job, bullet, project, and award the user has done, each tagged and carrying an "ownership rung" (1-6) that caps how confidently a bullet can ever describe the work. Read corpus/master-resume.yaml directly to understand its shape before reviewing the code that consumes it.

Start by reading README.md and CLAUDE.md in the project root — CLAUDE.md is the standing rules file (truthfulness constraints, scope discipline, output rules) and is binding on how this codebase must behave, not just a style guide. Violating one of those rules in the actual pipeline behavior counts as a bug, not a preference.

THE PIPELINE (all in scripts/)
    corpus.py     loads and validates master-resume.yaml
    matching.py   job posting -> tags (skill tags + domain tags) + evidence
    selection.py  tags -> filtered content. Bullet-level filtering by tag overlap,
                  plus a per-role cap (MAX_BULLETS_PER_ROLE, currently 6) that ranks
                  surviving bullets by tag-overlap count so one heavily-tagged
                  employer can't crowd out shorter, equally relevant ones.
    compose.py    OPTIONAL. Sends the already-selected bullets (post-cap) to Claude
                  (claude-opus-5) to merge, split, reorder, or rephrase them to match
                  how THIS SPECIFIC posting frames the work. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
                  in .env at the project root (already present and working).
    verify.py     mechanically checks every Claude-composed bullet against the exact
                  source text it cited — numbers, proper nouns, verb rank — before
                  it's allowed onto a resume. Anything that fails falls back to the
                  original deterministic bullet. A role only swaps in composed bullets
                  if EVERY proposed bullet for that role passes; no partial mixing.
    build.py      filtered/composed selection -> HTML matching the real design template
    render.py     HTML -> PDF + PNG page images
    ats.py        the SAME selection -> plain single-column .docx (built-in Word
                  styles only) for job-portal auto-fill parsers
    apply.py      CLI entry point / the function serve.py's web UI also calls
    serve.py      web UI (localhost:8020)

WHAT YOU'RE REVIEWING FOR

1. TOKEN / COST EFFICIENCY ON THE CLAUDE API SIDE
   Look specifically at scripts/compose.py: the system prompt, what gets sent per
   request (is it sending anything redundant or unnecessarily verbose?), the model
   choice (claude-opus-5) and whether it's justified for this task versus a cheaper
   model, the thinking config, MAX_TOKENS, and whether the request is scoped tightly
   to what's actually needed. Confirm composition only ever runs on the post-selection,
   post-cap bullet set (not the whole corpus) — verify that's actually true in the
   code, not just intended. Flag anything that burns tokens without improving output.

2. GENERAL CODE REVIEW FOR BUGS
   Go through every file in scripts/ plus template/ and the web UI. Look for actual
   defects — logic errors, edge cases that break the pipeline, error handling gaps,
   places where the code's behavior contradicts its own docstrings or CLAUDE.md's
   rules (e.g., verify.py failing to catch something it claims to catch, selection.py
   producing inconsistent results, a role that could still exceed the bullet cap
   under some path you find). Also flag anything that's a security or correctness risk
   even if unlikely to trigger today.

3. THE CORE TAILORING PHILOSOPHY — THIS IS IMPORTANT
   The goal of this program is not to mechanically dump every matching bullet onto a
   resume. It's to produce the BEST possible resume for one specific job posting. That
   means Claude, when composing, should feel free to combine multiple bullets into one
   when that reads better for a given posting, or take several related accomplishments
   and summarize them into a tighter, higher-impact line, rather than always keeping
   them as separate granular bullets. Review scripts/compose.py's SYSTEM_PROMPT and
   confirm it actually encourages this kind of judgment rather than just permitting
   narrow merges. Also think architecturally: right now selection.py's bullet cap
   (tag-overlap ranking) runs BEFORE composition ever sees the bullets — consider
   whether that's the right order, or whether composition would produce a better
   result if it could see a larger pool of relevant bullets and do the trimming
   itself via merging/summarizing, rather than a mechanical pre-cut deciding what
   Claude never even gets to consider. Give me your actual opinion on this, not just
   a description of how it currently works.

CURRENT PROJECT STATE — CONTEXT YOU NEED
- We are ONLY focused on getting the resume engine (PDF + ATS docx) working right now.
  Cover letters are explicitly out of scope and have not been started — do not flag
  their absence as a gap, it's expected.
- corpus/master-resume.yaml is intentionally incomplete — roughly 95% of the user's
  work history is compiled in and verified, with some known gaps (e.g., a recent
  documentary project not yet interviewed). This is fine and expected for testing.
  Do not treat corpus content gaps as a bug; only flag it if the CODE mishandles
  missing/partial data in a way that breaks the pipeline.
- The immediate next step after your review is running this against a real job
  posting for the first time, so the priority is: will this work correctly and
  efficiently when that happens.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU AT THE END
A clear summary with three sections:
1. WHAT WORKS — what you verified is solid and ready.
2. BUGS — anything you found, ranked by severity. If none, say so plainly, don't
   manufacture minor nitpicks to seem thorough.
3. QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS — concrete changes that would make the actual resume OUTPUT
   better (not just code cleanliness) — especially anything related to token
   efficiency and the merge/summarize tailoring behavior described above.

Do not make any code changes yourself. This is a review only — report findings back
so they can be discussed and approved before anything is touched.
Take this information and put forward a plan to fix all of these bugs and in what order you would fix them.
